title: [Research] Targeted Deleveraging of rsETH and osETH Through Exchange Rate Growth Discounting
headline: A research post by TokenLogic suggests setting the CAPO growth cap to 0% on rsETH and osETH as a more targeted alternative to raising the WETH borrow rate.
summary: TokenLogic's research post responds to LlamaRisk's ARFC on repositioning Aave V3 Core around established and liquid collateral, which lists a WETH borrow rate increase as a final follow-up control for rsETH and osETH loops if voluntary migration is insufficient. The post argues a WETH rate increase would raise borrowing costs across roughly $3.4B of WETH debt to address roughly $860M of rsETH and osETH loop exposure, and would also affect wstETH and weETH positions the ARFC intends to retain. As an alternative, it proposes setting maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent to 0% on the rsETH and osETH CAPO adapters, which freezes the maximum exchange rate Aave's oracle recognizes at its snapshot; this does not change the assets' actual redemption value. For rsETH, it also describes sized E-Mode liquidation threshold reductions after an initial borrower engagement and migration window. Open questions include how leveraged borrowers would be affected and how this fits with the ARFC's migration route.
risk_flags: changes oracle parameters on leveraged collateral
